steps.say: Age defines this disease before any gene result returns. Very early onset IBD means diagnosis under six years, infantile disease under two years, and neonatal disease under twenty eight days. The younger the gut, the likelier a single gene drives it. Date the onset precisely at referral, because an early birthday pushes the child straight onto the monogenic pathway.
steps.tx: The **age definition of VEO-IBD** sorts referrals before any sequencing returns. Very early onset IBD is diagnosis under **6 years**, infantile IBD under **2 years**, and neonatal IBD under **28 days** of life. Younger onset means higher odds of a single gene driver, so the birthday alone decides whether the child follows the standard biologic ladder or the monogenic workup.

steps.say: A baby with severe perianal fistulas who ignores anti-TNF drugs carries an interleukin 10 defect until proven otherwise. Loss of IL10 or its receptor removes the brakes from gut inflammation, producing penetrating infantile colitis with relentless perianal disease. Standard biologics fail because the missing signal sits upstream of TNF. Recognise the pattern and stop escalating blindly.
steps.tx: **IL-10 and IL-10R defects** explain the infant who never responds to biologics. Loss of function in **IL10**, **IL10RA**, or **IL10RB** unleashes hyperinflammatory, penetrating colitis with severe **perianal fistulae**, highly resistant to **anti-TNF** therapy. The missing anti-inflammatory signal sits upstream of every biologic target, so dose escalation only burns time while fistulas deepen.

steps.say: Stem cell transplant cures interleukin 10 deficiency outright. Allogeneic haematopoietic transplant replaces the broken immune compartment, healing both intestinal and perianal disease completely. Timing is everything: transplant before growth failure and surgical damage accumulate. Once the gene result confirms the defect, the gastroenterologist hands the child to the transplant team without delay.
steps.tx: **Curative HSCT in IL-10 receptor defect** makes genetics an emergency, not an academic exercise. Allogeneic **haematopoietic stem cell transplantation** replaces the defective immune system and resolves intestinal plus **perianal disease** completely. Transplant before growth failure and fistula surgery scar the child, so a confirmed IL-10 pathway defect triggers immediate transplant referral.

steps.say: Diabetes plus eczema plus watery diarrhoea in a boy spells IPEX. FOXP3 mutations erase regulatory T cells, so the immune system attacks gut, pancreas, and skin together. The enteropathy is severe and starts in infancy, with type 1 diabetes and eczema completing the triad. Immunosuppression bridges the child to transplant, which is the only lasting fix.
steps.tx: **IPEX syndrome genetics** unite three organs in one acronym. **FOXP3** mutation destroys regulatory **T-cell** control, giving immunodysregulation with **enteropathy**, polyendocrinopathy including type 1 diabetes, and eczema, X-linked in boys. Severe infantile diarrhoea plus diabetes plus eczema should trigger FOXP3 testing at once, since sirolimus bridges to curative transplant.

steps.say: Refractory Crohn-like colitis that spirals into HLH points at XIAP. This X linked inhibitor of apoptosis defect produces severe perianal disease plus a terrifying tendency to haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Fevers with cytopenias in such a child are HLH until proven otherwise. Standard IBD drugs cannot fix the killing defect, so transplant planning starts at diagnosis.
steps.tx: **XIAP deficiency** turns colitis into a transplant emergency. Loss of X-linked inhibitor of apoptosis gives refractory **Crohn-like colitis** with severe perianal disease plus high susceptibility to **haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis** (HLH). Fever with falling blood counts in these boys means HLH workup first, IBD escalation never, and early transplant planning.

points: HSCT cures bowel and perianal disease
left.title: IL-10 defect pattern

steps.say: Sequence every child with IBD under six before any biologic escalation. A comprehensive targeted panel or whole exome test must precede anti-TNF, because a monogenic answer reroutes the child to transplant or targeted therapy instead. Spending the budget on a biologic that cannot work is the costliest error. No panel, no biologic is the rule in this age group.
steps.tx: The **next-generation sequencing panel** is mandatory before biologics in the very young. Comprehensive targeted gene or **whole-exome sequencing** must precede any escalation in IBD under **6 years**, since a monogenic answer diverts the child toward transplant or pathway therapy. Biologics started blind waste months and mask the real diagnosis, so sequence first and prescribe second.

steps.say: Atresias plus immunodeficiency in a neonate implicate TTC7A. These mutations produce multiple intestinal atresia with apoptotic enterocolitis alongside severe combined immunodeficiency, a combination no sporadic disease explains. Transplant fixes the immune half but leaves the epithelial defect untouched, so gut failure persists. Counsel the family that two diseases share one gene and only one is curable.
steps.tx: **TTC7A epithelial defect** splits the prognosis in two. **TTC7A** mutations cause multiple intestinal **atresia** with apoptotic enterocolitis plus severe combined **immunodeficiency**. HSCT corrects the immune failure yet cannot repair the **epithelial defect**, so diarrhoea and dependence persist after a successful transplant. Families need this split prognosis before consenting.

rows: HSCT does not cure the gut

steps.say: Granulomas plus sinopulmonary infections plus colitis mean chronic granulomatous disease. CYBB or NCF mutations cripple the phagocyte burst, and thirty to forty percent develop Crohn-like colitis. Reaching for anti-TNF here invites fatal fungal infection, because the granuloma already holds fungi poorly. Treat the colitis with steroids or immunomodulators and plan transplant.
steps.tx: **Chronic granulomatous disease colitis** punishes blind anti-TNF use. **CYBB** or **NCF** mutations disable the neutrophil burst, and Crohn-like colitis strikes **30-40%** of patients. **Anti-TNF therapy** in CGD sharply raises fatal **fungal infection** risk, so colitis needs steroids or immunomodulators while the team plans HSCT. Recurrent abscesses plus colitis should trigger dihydrorhodamine testing.
